tasks.short: Interview employers and employees about workplace incidents

steps.what: Locate the actual workplace incident file and relevant work-environment records in {DOCS} before the interview.
inputs: Existing incident id and permitted case records

steps.what: Interview employers and employees about work environments and workplace incidents, following their accounts and probing uncertainties without leading the witness.
outputs: Actual account, distinctions and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write the actual interview note in {DOCS}, distinguishing reported statements, observations and the engineer's interpretation.
inputs: Actual account and uncertainties from s2
outputs: Actual interview note with attribution and uncertainty

steps.what: Save the interview note in the same restricted {DOCS} case workspace.

tasks.design: Configure the existing incident-id view in {DOCS} to find permitted background records. The engineer conducts the interview and writes the actual account; there is no inferred testimony, recording requirement or approval stage for saving the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case context can be spread across incident and workplace records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native restricted case views can reduce navigation while preserving original sources.
tasks.still_hard: Fear, memory and conflicting accounts require careful human questioning.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, distinguish evidence from inference and notice what needs clarification.

ambition.what: Keep the interview focused on the actual account.

tasks.altitude: Only context retrieval changes; investigative authority stays the same.

reach.learn: Use non-leading questions and preserve the provenance of reported exposure information.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for restricted case permissions and national consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Restricted document views can group existing case records; they cannot establish the truth of an interviewee's account.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual interview preparation, questioning and the separate interview note. No new transcript or witness-approval administration is assumed.

Existing case owners provide incident id, document id, version and access classification. s1 verifies relevance manually. Records without reliable metadata are located and read manually, with no claimed reduction for those sources.

Conditional E1 activity estimates. Only navigation within s1 changes, not substantive reading. Native access-filtered views are tested first. The same-system save remains at 1%, fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Do incident records have reliable case identifiers and appropriate access restrictions?
research_questions: Can the engineer find permitted context without exposing unrelated health or witness data?

already_counted.description: Context checks, actual interview and note writing

incremental.description: Check restricted case-view metadata and permissions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 2 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5. Conservative case: witness-sensitive records cannot be grouped safely, so the engineer retains the existing manual context search and does not install the view; questioning and note writing are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find the actual permitted evidence bundle, engineering records and cited document versions in {DOCS} for the litigation case.
inputs: Actual case instructions and existing evidence bundle

steps.what: Critically assess the actual evidence, engineering methods, competing explanations and limits of the expert's own competence.
Write the actual expert opinion and source-linked working notes in {DOCS}, preserving the distinction between facts, assumptions and conclusions.
outputs: Actual expert opinion and working notes

steps.what: Save the expert working documents in the same restricted {DOCS} workspace.
inputs: Actual opinion and notes from s3

steps.what: Provide the actual expert testimony in the proceeding, explaining the opinion and answering challenges within the evidence and expertise available.
outputs: Expert testimony and clarification of its limits

tasks.design: Use native source and version indexes in {DOCS} for the actual evidence bundle. Expert assessment, written opinion and testimony remain human; no model creates authorities, decides causation or answers questions in the proceeding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating the exact evidence version can interrupt preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexes can link the original material and version identifiers without changing its meaning.
tasks.still_hard: An independent opinion must withstand incomplete evidence and adversarial questioning.
tasks.human_edge: Explain defensible engineering reasoning and candidly state what cannot be concluded.

ambition.what: Preserve evidence traceability for the existing expert task.

tasks.altitude: Small retrieval improvement; expert responsibility is unchanged.

reach.learn: Separate engineering mechanisms from unsupported causal assertions.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for case confidentiality and permitted evidence handling

evidence.claim: A versioned evidence index can reduce navigation while leaving expert assessment and testimony human.

assumptions: Boundary is actual expert preparation, working opinion and testimony. The expert's working-document save is ordinary internal storage, not a court filing; any separately required filing retains its existing authorised process and no saving is claimed for it.

The actual evidence bundle already has original files and case document identifiers. s1 checks version and provenance; missing or disputed identifiers require manual inspection. No uncounted OCR, case-law research or generated citation feed is assumed.

Conditional E1 activity shares. Native indexing is tested before code. Only locating evidence changes; critical reading and all opinion writing remain fully retained. Internal saving has no self-approval gate.
unknowns: Is the evidence bundle already indexed?
What evidence handling is permitted for this case?
research_questions: Does source navigation improve without obscuring contradictory evidence or document versions?

already_counted.description: Source verification, independent assessment, opinion writing and actual testimony

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 3 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5. Conservative case: a supplied litigation bundle already has exact navigation and version links; retain that bundle and all substantive expert work with no additional index or labour claim.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review adequacy of employee safety programs

steps.what: Retrieve actual employee safety programs, revision records and supporting training or inspection evidence from {DOCS}.
inputs: Existing actual safety program and supporting records

steps.what: Map actual workplace hazards to the program's intended controls and identify the explicit evidence required for this review in {DOCS}.
inputs: Actual hazard assessments and applicable requirements

steps.what: Match the required evidence identifiers against the available record identifiers and revision fields using native {DOCS} lists.
inputs: Actual record identifiers and revisions from s1

steps.what: Review whether the employee safety program actually controls the workplace hazards, testing the substance of the evidence and investigating gaps.
outputs: Engineer assessment of program adequacy and limitations

steps.what: Write the actual adequacy findings and needed corrective actions in {DOCS}.
Save the review findings in the same {DOCS} workspace.

tasks.design: Configure native {DOCS} retrieval and an exact required-record comparison. The comparison reports document presence and revision mismatches only; the engineer determines safety-program adequacy and writes the findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual document matching competes with substantive safety review.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured document identifiers support literal comparison against a human-authored evidence list.
tasks.still_hard: Document presence says little about whether a control works in practice.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the connection between real hazards, controls and evidence of effectiveness.

ambition.what: Re-examine a changed hazard's control evidence after an actual process change.

tasks.altitude: Less clerical evidence matching; no automatic adequacy decision.

reach.learn: Connect process changes to actual safety-control evidence.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for restricted records and national consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Exact record-id and revision comparisons can flag missing evidence without assessing the adequacy of a safety program.

assumptions: Boundary includes evidence assembly, hazard/control mapping, adequacy judgement and the actual written review. No new sign-off process is created.

Record owners already supply document id, program id and revision. s2 produces the actual required ids and applicability decisions. s3 performs only exact matches, not semantic compliance interpretation. Unstructured or ambiguous evidence remains manually compared in s4.
Conditional E1 time estimates, not measured savings. Native lists are tested first and existing automatic comparisons earn no benefit. Same-system saving is fully retained at 1% without a gate.
unknowns: Are control evidence and revisions identified consistently?
research_questions: Can the comparison flag a missing revision without implying that a complete record set establishes adequate controls?

already_counted.description: Source checks, hazard mapping, substantive adequacy review and actual findings

incremental.description: Maintain identifier matching and test revision exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 4.5 retrieval plus 10 literal matching = 14.5; minus 1 upkeep gives 13.5. Conservative case: evidence is mostly narrative and has no stable identifiers, so both navigation and matching remain manual and the configuration is not adopted. The 40-share adequacy review and actual findings remain in all cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise organizations on health-related workplace changes

steps.what: Clarify the actual health-related workplace problem, affected work and proposed changes with the organization.
inputs: Actual organization's problem and operating context

steps.what: Locate relevant current technical guidance and permitted workplace evidence in {DOCS}.
inputs: Current technical guidance and actual workplace evidence

steps.what: Determine appropriate technical advice and guidance for handling the health-related problem, including limits and needs for specialist assessment.
inputs: Actual problem and constraints from s1

steps.what: Write the actual technical advice, evidence, proposed changes and uncertainties in {DOCS}.
Explain the technical guidance to the organization and discuss practical changes, uncertainties and questions.
Save the actual advice record in the same restricted {DOCS} workspace.

tasks.design: Configure native current-guidance views in {DOCS} to reduce navigation for the engineer. Advice formation, actual written guidance and discussion stay human; this does not diagnose an individual or automatically change workplace controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current applicable technical source interrupts case-specific advice.
tasks.enabler_now: Native topic and version filters can expose original approved guidance.
tasks.still_hard: Suitable controls depend on actual exposure, work practices and implementation constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Turn technical evidence into realistic changes and explain the limits honestly.

ambition.what: Offer supervised technical guidance sessions to small operational teams facing a newly identified exposure issue.

tasks.altitude: Less source navigation; professional advice rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Connect workplace exposure routes to environmental source controls.

evidence.claim: Approved-source navigation can be configured without delegating health-related technical advice to a model.

assumptions: Boundary covers actual consultation, evidence reading, technical advice writing and explanation. No invented recurring report or internal approval stage is added.

Existing guidance owners provide topic, document id, version and applicability. The engineer supplies the actual question in s1 and checks relevance in s2. Missing metadata means ordinary manual reading; no uncounted extraction or personal health-data feed is assumed.
Conditional E1 activity estimates; only navigation changes. Native configuration is tested first. The internal save has its small retained time and no approval gate.
unknowns: Is approved current guidance available for the actual problems?
research_questions: Can the engineer find relevant guidance while preserving the distinction between technical workplace advice and individual clinical assessment?

already_counted.description: Actual consultation, source checking, recommendation, written guidance and discussion

incremental.description: Check guidance-version filters after source revisions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 3.75 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 3.25; high rounded down to 3.2. Conservative case: an unusual exposure needs sources outside the approved collection, so the engineer retains the complete manual source search and does not adopt this view for that case; advice writing and discussion remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: An engineer who finds evidence more directly while retaining interviews, expert testimony and safety judgement.
reach: Connect workplace exposure evidence with environmental engineering assessments
role.ambitious_version: More traceable technical guidance with the same human responsibility for safety conclusions.

job.title: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
